Nov 11, 2026/8 min readIndustry Solutions
Moving AI from Pilot to P&L: What Finance Leaders Should Take Away From Expedition 2026
Snowflake
Snowflake
Statistics of business concept. Finance chart. Financial planning. Data analysis.
The month-end close has become the proving ground for AI in finance. Day 3 of Snowflake Expedition 2026 was built for the office of the CFO, with sessions featuring learnings from finance leaders who have moved AI into the work that defines their teams: closing the books, explaining variance, reforecasting, testing controls and preparing the tax provision.
Across every session, speakers made the same point in different ways. Finance will adopt AI when it can trust the output, and that trust comes from governed data, clear ownership and a human in the loop wherever judgment is required.
If you missed the live virtual event — or if you attended and want a little refresher — here are seven sessions that CFOs, chief accounting officers and finance executives will find useful as you start planning for next year. You can also check out the entire agenda track for finance leaders for more strategic and technical sessions on incorporating AI into your financial team workflows.
Leading the shift from control function to growth partner
Finance teams are being asked to close faster, forecast with more confidence and advise the business in near real time, while also proving that AI investments pay off. These three sessions describe what that shift looks like and how leaders are managing it.
The AI Blueprint for Finance Teams
In the Day 3 opening keynote, Snowflake CFO Brian Robins shares his view of the trends and pressures shaping the finance function. Yasmeen Ahmad, Senior Vice President and GM of Data Cloud at Workday, introduces zero-copy integration between Workday Data Cloud and Snowflake, which makes Workday data directly available in Snowflake. Gordon Lee, Chief Accounting Officer at DoorDash, offers a Snowflake customer’s perspective on the impact of AI-driven finance workflows and how integrated data infrastructure, governance and permissions enables his team to use data more effectively. The keynote closes with a walkthrough of how Snowflake's own finance team runs on Snowflake, then follows a CFO through a continuous close cycle that runs from accelerating the close and explaining variance to reforecasting and preparing for earnings.
This session is a must-watch for any financial leadership team. It presents a shared, end-to-end picture of an AI-enabled close, which makes it much easier to agree on where your own team should start.
Watch “The AI Blueprint for Finance Teams” now.

SNOW Q2 Earnings Call Highlights AI Flywheel, Higher Outlook
Snowflake Inc. SNOW used its second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call to emphasize accelerating AI adoption, stronger core-platform consumption and a higher full-year product revenue outlook. Management framed AI as a multiplier across new workloads, users and existing customer spending.
The reported quarter also cleared Zacks expectations. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.62 beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.45, while revenues of $1.54 billion topped the $1.47 billion consensus.
Snowflake Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Snowflake Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
Snowflake Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Snowflake Inc. Quote
Chief financial officer Brian Robins raised fiscal 2027 product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion, representing 36% year-over-year growth, from the prior $5.84 billion and 31% growth outlook.
For the fiscal third quarter, Robins guided product revenues to $1.588 billion-$1.593 billion or 37-38% growth. He said forecasts continue to rely on observed consumption patterns rather than a changed methodology.
Snowflake also lifted full-year non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 14.5% from 13.5%, while reiterating 23% adjusted free cash flow margin guidance.
Snowflake Ties AI to Core Consumption
Chief executive officer Sridhar Ramaswamy said AI is strengthening Snowflake through new workloads, adoption of CoCo and CoWork, and higher broader platform consumption by customers using AI.
In the Q&A session, an Evercore ISI analyst asked how much of the acceleration came from newer AI products versus the core business. Ramaswamy said AI products contributed approximately half, with core products and faster migrations supplying the rest.
Robins added that fiscal second-quarter product revenues rose 37% year over year, marking a third straight quarter of acceleration, with strength across both the core data platform and AI revenues.
SNOW Deepens Agent Adoption and Customer Reach
Ramaswamy said CoCo surpassed 9,100 accounts after adding more than 2,000 during the second quarter, while CoWork expanded to 5,800 accounts.
He also highlighted customer use cases spanning data migration, sales, finance and supply-chain processes. Snowflake added 692 net new customers, including 14 net new Forbes Global 2000 customers.
Robins said net revenue retention was 126%, while 828 customers generated more than $1 million in trailing 12-month product revenues. Remaining performance obligations reached $9 billion, up 30% year over year.
Snowflake Faces Q&A on Growth Quality
A Morgan Stanley analyst pressed management on whether the acceleration was broad and durable. Ramaswamy said growth came from a broad customer base and that AI-native companies remained a small share of revenue.
He also stressed that CoCo can help customers optimize queries and warehouse usage, supporting more…[truncated]
